newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares tumble, index ends 1.75 percent down.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares tumble, index ends 1.75 percent down.

text.p: ** (1005 GMT) - Bombay shares take a beating to end lower
as speculators unwind positions in blue chip stocks
** Bombay's benchmark index loses 59.14 pts, or 1.75 pct to
3,323.33, provisional close, off 3,382.47
** Failed government promises affect market sentiments with
lack of buyers prompting a slide in prices
** Bank stock SBI down 4.60 pct on heavy speculative
selling, operators offload huge built-up positions
** Index heavy weights tumble, lack of buying support seen
** National Stock Exchange extends trading hours by 30
minutes to 1600 local time (1100 GMT)
A spate of speculative sell-orders put pressure on Bombay blue chips on Monday, pulling down the benchmark index 1.75 percent by close, dealers said.
"Speculators are running for cover. The lack of buyers is hitting the market hard," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.
Traders said an absence of positive news after the government last week failed to announce promised market policy initiatives weighed heavy on minds of major players.
"Everyone's disappointed and frustrated with the market. The speculators have all gone quiet," said the chief dealer at a London-based broking firm.
Share prices rose sharply in January on frequent assurances by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda that his government would unveil a series of new market-friendly policy initiaties.
But Finance Minister P. Chidambaram dashed hopes last week when he said the expected package actually consisted of measures already taken since January.
Bombay's index reacted sharply, plunging 127.58 points, or 3.6 percent, to 3382.47 on Friday.
Analysts said they were advising investors to pick up stocks at declines. "The mood now is to only look for specific good stock ideas," said Alok Sethi, director at Natwest Securities.
At the Bombay Stock Exchange, SBI lost 12.50 rupees, or 4.60 percent to close at 259.0 in volumes of 6.78 million shares.
Reliance was down 9.25 rupees to 255.25, TISCO 3.25 to 178.50, ITC 8.0 to 376.25 and TELCO 10.70 to 308.25.
Pivotals fell further at the National Stock Exchange with the 50-stock ending 25.0 points, or 2.6 percent, down to a provisional 946.40. SBI ended 18.60 rupees or 6.8 percent.
"A lot of stock is getting liquidated...there has also been some fund-based selling," said Dilip Joshi, dealer at local firm Prime Broking.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
